title: God Used a Murderer: Moses’ Story
paragraphs: God Used a Murderer: Moses’ Story
He killed a man.

Not accidentally.
Not symbolically.
Moses saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew slave…
And he looked both ways.
“You knew.”
Then he struck the man down and buried him in the sand.
God saw it.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The sand did not hide Moses’ sin.
It only delayed the moment he had to face it.
Exodus 2:12 says, “He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.”
Read that again.

He checked for people.
Not for God.

That is what sin does.
It teaches you to fear exposure more than holiness.

Moses ran.
From Egypt.
From Pharaoh.
From his past.
From the blood on his hands.
But he could not outrun the God who calls sinners by name.
Years later, God met him in the wilderness through a burning bush.

Not a palace.
Not a platform.
A wilderness.
Because sometimes God strips you down before He sends you out.
Moses said, “Who am I?”
But God did not answer with Moses’ greatness.
He answered with His presence.
“I will be with you.” — Exodus 3:12
That is grace.

Not God pretending Moses never sinned.
Not God excusing murder.
Not God lowering His holiness.
Grace means God can take a guilty man, confront him, cleanse him, and commission him.

Moses was not saved because he became useful.
He became useful because God showed mercy.
And this points to Jesus.
Because Moses delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt…
But Jesus delivers sinners from slavery to sin.
Romans 3:23 says, “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
Romans 6:23 says, “The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
You may not have buried a body in the sand.

But you have buried lies.
Lust.
Pride.
Bitterness.
Secret rebellion.
That thing you keep explaining away.
God saw it.
And still, Jesus came.

Christ did not die for cleaned-up people.
He died for sinners.
“While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
So repent.

Stop hiding in the wilderness of shame.
Stop calling conviction “negativity.”
Stop thinking your past is stronger than the blood of Jesus.
Moses’ story is not proof that sin does not matter.
It is proof that grace is greater.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
